subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & rate limits
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>; Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Raj / Sarah,

Thanks again for your time today — great to meet the Acme Health team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our demo: 

What we covered:
- Hosted API quickstart (API keys, example endpoints, streaming)
- Typical rate/throughput tradeoffs and where Dedicated/Private can fit in
- Security basics (VPC, KMS options for Private)

Immediate next steps I can help with:
1) Provide a short quickstart guide and a temporary eval key so your engineers can run sample prompts against the Hosted API.
2) Capture expected traffic profile (peak RPS, typical request size in tokens, concurrency) so we can confirm whether Hosted will meet SLA or if Dedicated capacity makes sense.
3) If PHI/HIPAA is in scope, we should flag Private deployment early — we can still do an initial eval on Hosted but will discuss Private options and timeline.

Quick technical notes (Hosted API):
- REST endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Example curl (non-streaming):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model": "redwood-1.1", "prompt": "Summarize patient note...", "max_tokens": 256}'
- Streaming and SSE are supported from the same endpoint — see the quickstart doc attached.
- Default Hosted rate limits (apply per-account / can be increased for trials): 250 requests/sec, up to 500k tokens/minute. We can provision higher throughput for enterprise evals or recommend Dedicated if you need predictable sustained throughput above that.

Attachment: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (attached)
Related docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart

Can you share the traffic/latency targets (peak RPS, average request size in tokens, acceptable p50/p95 latency)? I can spin up a temporary eval key and loop in Aditya (SE) to help with the quickstart call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

--
This message and attachments are intended for the named recipients only.

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Thanks Neha — appreciated the demo. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic profile: peak ~200 RPS for inference requests during business hours (multi-tenant across product), average prompt size ~120 tokens, peaks up to ~400 tokens. Concurrent users typically spike briefly.
- Latency targets: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 600ms for typical prompts.
- Data sensitivity: our workload will include PHI (patient notes) — so HIPAA is in scope. We need to understand if the Hosted API is compatible or whether we should plan for Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Trial access: can you provide a temporary key and sample curl examples? Also want to test streaming for interactive workflows.

If Hosted can handle the numbers with appropriate encryption/controls, we'd prefer to start there for speed, then evaluate Dedicated/Private for production.

Thanks,
Raj
Director of Product
Acme Health
raj.patel@acmehealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>; Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Raj — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Short answers up front:

- Throughput: peak 200 RPS (with 120 tokens avg) is within our Hosted evaluation envelope. Our default Hosted quota is 250 RPS and 500k tokens/min; for a short-term eval we can raise those limits to match your peaks. Sustained, predictable heavy workloads or strict SLOs are typically best on Dedicated.
- Latency: based on the model profile we demoed, p50/p95 targets you listed are achievable on Hosted in our US regions; we'll validate with your exact prompts.
- PHI/HIPAA: Hosted can be used for initial evals but for HIPAA-covered production workloads we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) — that said, we can support a HIPAA-ready Private deployment timeline in parallel. For the eval, if you prefer to avoid sending PHI to Hosted, you can scrub or synthetic-ize a subset of examples and we can test on those.

I've attached the quickstart guide (redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf) and created a temporary eval key for your team: https://app.redwood.ai/eval/temporary-key/ACME-042 (valid for 14 days). The key will have increased Hosted quotas for the evaluation window.

Example streaming (node):
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <TEMP_KEY>', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-1.1', prompt: '...streaming prompt...', stream: true })
});
// handle SSE/chunks as they arrive

Next steps:
- Try the quickstart with the temp key and share p95/p50 latency numbers + token counts for a few representative prompts.
- If you'd like, Aditya can run a 30-minute quickstart session this week to walk engineers through the integration and streaming tests.

Can you confirm a time that works for the quickstart pairing? I'm flexible Thu/Fri morning PST or Tue next week.

Best,
Neha

Attachment: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf

Aditya / Marissa — looping you both in. Raj from Acme Health has HIPAA in scope and will run an eval (synthetic/scrubbed data preferred). They indicated ~200 RPS peaks and p95 < 600ms targets.

Can Aditya lead the quickstart pairing (streaming + perf checks) and confirm whether we should recommend Hosted with elevated quotas vs pushing for Private/Dedicated sooner? If Aditya thinks Hosted is viable for an eval, can you prepare a short checklist:

- Any config tweaks (batching, prompt chunking, model/quantization) to meet p95

Neha
